messages:
maya: starting a quick thread for TritonFlare-7B quant smoke — seeing intermittent OOMs when max_new_tokens >= 1024, and memory fragmentation on warmup. can ppl share latest smoke results?
zach: saw the same on canary yesterday. pattern: initial requests fine, after ~300s of steady traffic we get a spike and then OOMs on large requests. logs show repeated allocation failures from slab allocator.
linh: pushed a smoke run with int4 and prefetched KV enabled. attached logs:
```
[2026-02-15T14:02:11Z] slab_free: reclaimed 12MB
[2026-02-15T14:02:12Z] alloc: gpu_mem_alloc failed size=120MB context=generate.delayed
[2026-02-15T14:02:12Z] OOM at sequence=1034 max_new=1500 model=tritonflare-7b-int4
```
manually trimmed. ops-bot: triage note created: INC-9872 linking canary cluster.
man: (typo, ignore)
anita: hypothesis: comb of large max_new_tokens + continuous batching causing allocation churn and fragmentation. propose two quick mitigations to test: 1) lower default max_new_tokens to 512 for TF-7B int4, 2) enable soft-evict for KV and increase microbatch timeout to 120ms to reduce tail allocations.
maya: can you add an experiment matrix? small runs only.
linh: experiment matrix posted to /tmp on the canary host and to the eval harness: 3 runs each: (A) max_new=512 + microbatch=120ms, (B) max_new=1024 + soft-evict on, (C) max_new=512 + prefetch off.

zach: quick results summary after two runs each:
- A: no OOMs, tail p99 latency +8% (expected), token throughput -4%
- B: 2 OOMs during steady-state, fragmentation still shows in slab metrics
- C: no OOMs, latency worse p50 +15% but p99 similar to A

maya: useful. eval-bot: posted eval diffs for quality on flagship prompts (A vs baseline int4):
```
- Perplexity: delta +0.4
- RougeL: delta -0.3
- Few-shot QA accuracy: unchanged within noise
```

anita: sounds like safest default is A (max_new 512 + microbatch 120ms + soft-evict enabled). tradeoff: slight latency and tiny quality delta. recommend rollout to canary with 2x canaries and 24h smoke.

linh: I'll open a PR to change model defaults and add rollout config (canary=2, rollback on OOM>0 or p99 latency regression >20%). PR will include memory and slab charts.

zach: quick note — add a telemetry tag so we can break down by prompt length and session reuse. without that we won't know if some prompts trigger frag.
maya: agreed. assign to lin h to add tag.

anita: ok; after canary run we'll decide a permanent default. thanks team :thumbsup:
